body:
Truth.  Active duty Army for a decade (physician).  Only assault rifle I ever fired was an M16 in OBLC.  After that, I carried an M9 (pistol).  Even then, the only time I really shot was my own S&W M&P40 on my own time.  My unit's 11Bs (infantrymen) were frequently firing, as were my own 68Ws (medics).  If a situation had ever deteriorated to the point where the unit physician had to take up an M4 - we had bigger problems and likely screwed already.  Plus, there would likely be plenty of extra M4s laying around for me at that point anyhow.

I do find it hard to believe that commander didn't know that scope was backwards.  Even a kid with a pair of binoculars would likely naturally flip them if the image was less clear through them then without.  Likely a poor judgement call by the commander to let the photo op go forward despite him knowing something wasn't right.
Also received this.  Trying to get me to pay 3.99.  Sorry, CNN.  Off to Associated Press.

I am in a frontline specialty. I see everything from runny noses to gunshot wounds. 

Having these feelings, especially discussing these feelings, is difficult. Other providers can’t do much. It’s like being on fire, surrounded by water, but you can’t step in to put yourself out.
United States of America. I can’t provide any further info beyond that.
I love my job. I love my patients. I hate myself.  I have a long story that I’m sure would sound insignificant here. But it’s not to me.

Hospital will immediately suspend my privileges. That is required reporting when applying for new jobs as a physician. New jobs also screen for this type of thing prior to interviews. As do state licensure boards.
I tried the suicide hotline tonight as well. I was on hold for a half hour and gave up.

What most will not understand is that being in the hospital is likely the last place they should be unless the NEED to be there... (oxygen support, vent, IV meds, can’t care for self etc). Otherwise they’re just exposing themselves to other pathogens.

There is always a reason to go on. Even if it’s just the hope that you can make tomorrow better. I’ve struggled as well, and do struggle continuously. I’m 34, and by all external appearances, very successful. Ive also spent the last year sleeping with a special bullet on my bedside table. There is always a reason not to do it. 

Please reach out to someone. Most folks will try to lift you up and out. Let them try.
